subject: general
question:
If n is a natural number. then, for what value of k is the following function a probability mass function? 

 f(x)=(n!)/(x!(n-x)!)k^x(1-k)ⁿ⁻x, x=0,1,2....n
solution:
The correct answer is** k = 0.2**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** Probability Mass Function:

__
 
• A function f(x) is a probability mass function (PMF) if the sum of f(x) over all possible values of x equals 1.
 
• In this case, the given function is a binomial probability mass function: f(x)=n!x!(n−x)!kx(1−k)n−x" id="MathJax-Element-164-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">f(x)=n!x!(n−x)!kx(1−k)n−xf(x)=n!x!(n−x)!kx(1−k)n−x
 \rm f(x) = \frac{n!}{x!(n-x)!}k^x(1-k)^{n-x}
 .
 
• The sum of all binomial probabilities for a given n is always 1, provided k is the probability of success (0 ≤ k ≤ 1).
 
• Hence, the correct value of k should be a probability value (between 0 and 1).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 Let's analyze each option:

**Option 1: k = 0.2**

 
• 0.2 is a valid probability value (0 ≤ 0.2 ≤ 1).
 
• The sum of binomial probabilities with k = 0.2 will be 1.
 
• Hence, the function will be a valid PMF.

**Option 2: k = 10**

 
• 10 is not a valid probability value (10 > 1).
 
• The sum of binomial probabilities with k = 10 will not be 1.
 
• Hence, the function will not be a valid PMF.

**Option 3: k = 5**

 
• 5 is not a valid probability value (5 > 1).
 
• The sum of binomial probabilities with k = 5 will not be 1.
 
• Hence, the function will not be a valid PMF.

**Option 4: k = 2**

 
• 2 is not a valid probability value (2 > 1).
 
• The sum of binomial probabilities with k = 2 will not be 1.
 
• Hence, the function will not be a valid PMF.

***Hence, the correct value of k that makes the function a probability mass function is k = 0.2.***
